title: Cloud Spend by Tag or Project (Chargeback)

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.8 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.8 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via Combined cloud TAs, CUR, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Combined cloud TAs, CUR, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.8_cloud_spend_by_tag_or_pr_8"
| sort -_time
description: Allocating cost by tag (AWS/Azure) or project/label (GCP) enables chargeback and showback. Supports budget accountability and optimization by team.
value: Detecting cloud spend by tag or project (chargeback) early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest billing data with tag/project dimensions. Normalize tag keys (e.g. Owner, Team, Environment). Dashboard cost by tag/project and trend. Set budget alerts per tag/project. Reconcile with actual invoices.
visualization: Stacked bar (cost by tag value), Table (tag, cost, % of total), Line chart (cost trend by team).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Combined cloud TAs, CUR, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest billing data with tag/project dimensions. Normalize tag keys (e.g. Owner, Team, Environment). Dashboard cost by tag/project and trend. Set budget alerts per tag/project. Reconcile with actual invoices.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.8_cloud_spend_by_tag_or_pr_8"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=aws` to detect cloud spend by tag or project (chargeback). Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_8_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Stacked bar (cost by tag value), Table (tag, cost, % of total), Line chart (cost trend by team)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Combined cloud TAs, CUR, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud spend by tag or project (chargeback) so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
